sources.entry: watchfiles - Simple, modern and fast file watching and code reload in Python.

summary.one_liner: watchfiles is a Python library and CLI for watching files and directories for changes and reloading code, built on the Rust Notify library.
summary.what_it_does: Provides synchronous (watch) and asynchronous (awatch) generators that yield sets of file changes in a given directory. Provides run_process and arun_process, which run a target function in a separate process and restart it when files change. Includes a command-line tool that runs a given shell command and reloads it when files in a chosen path change. Underlying file system notifications are handled by the Notify rust library. The package was previously named watchgod, and the README points to a migration guide.
use_cases: auto-reload a Python app during development
watch a directory and react to file changes
run a shell command whenever source files change
async file watching in asyncio programs
restart a worker process on code edits
how_to_run: from watchfiles import watch; for changes in watch('./path/to/dir'): print(changes)
notable: Both sync (watch, run_process) and async (awatch, arun_process) APIs
Built-in CLI for running a command and reloading on changes
Prebuilt binaries for most architectures on Linux, macOS and Windows
Formerly named watchgod; migration guide provided
caveats: Installing from source requires Rust stable to be installed
